plan.for_the_user:
Here's the plan, short version. Three judges scored three plans, and this one won 93–87–82 over the other two. I've also added the best parts of the other two.

**What it does**
You say "make a steampunk teapot". Fable builds it in Blender, which runs hidden in the background, so you never see its window. The model pops into our app, and you sculpt it with your hands and voice. Then say "make the lid gold": Fable changes it and your sculpting stays.

**How it works**
- **Hidden Blender:** our server starts one hidden Blender. If it crashes it's back in about 3 seconds and nothing is lost.
- **What Fable checks:** Fable looks at renders of the exact file you'll get, so what it sees is what you see.
- **Lighting:** models get proper lighting, so gold actually looks like gold.
- **No 1:1 open-source sculptor exists.** The closest is three.js's brand-new Sculptor, but it's missing most of Blender's brushes and settings. We use it only for the mesh plumbing and port Blender's own brush code on top, with Blender's own default brush settings.
- **Checked against real Blender:** a script runs the real brushes in hidden Blender and compares the results with ours. The first port is already within 1.5%.
- **Nothing gets lost:** your edits go back into Blender before every Fable change, save or undo.

**With your hands and voice**
- Pinch = brush down, point = aim, two hands = turn and resize.
- Say a brush name ("clay strips", "grab", "scrape", "crease", "snake hook", "elastic grab", "smooth", "mask").
- Or say "bigger", "stronger", "invert", "mirror on", "undo", "redo", "add detail", "save version", "go back to version 3".

**Dropped**
- Your hand as Blender's mouse, the visible Blender window, and the old OpenAI part-list generator.
- Blender features that aren't worth porting here (cloth, multires, texture painting). For extrude, bevel or booleans, just ask Fable.

**3 decisions for you** (details and my picks below)
1. GPL licence and a public repo. This is required to port Blender's code. I recommend yes.
2. Should "make it red" go to Fable (1–4 min) or be instant?
3. Should "add detail right under the brush" come now or later? I recommend later.

Core build is about 24 hours of work across 7 steps. After step 3 you can already sculpt a Fable teapot with Blender brushes.
plan.architecture:
Chosen plan: best-hybrid ("HoloModel v3"), with grafts. The judges split: judge 1 picked web-truth (30 vs 28), judges 2 and 3 picked best-hybrid (32 and 33). Combined totals are best-hybrid 93, web-truth 87, blender-truth 82, so best-hybrid is the base.

Its two flaws are fixed:
- Parity is automated. I re-ran plan/parity/port_check2.mjs with RAY=orig INFN=orig: Draw 1.519%, half-pressure Draw 1.439%, Inflate 1.398% of Blender's max displacement. Default semantics give 4.136%.
- The from-scratch mesh core is replaced by the vendored three r186 SculptorMesh, already verified in Edge on r170 with the real Fable teapot.

THREE PROCESSES

1) BROWSER (Edge, three@0.170, all dependencies vendored locally): the only thing the user sees.
- scene/: GLB -> Part tree keyed by holo_id, display parent m->cm, per-part material clones, env map + AgX, overlay highlight, views[] render loop for the later Pepper's-ghost.
- sculpt/ ("holosculpt", GPL-3.0-or-later): Blender's stroke engine, StrokeCache, factor pipeline, symmetry and brush kernels, paraphrased from blender@235621e. It runs on a per-part welded proxy built on the forked MIT SculptorMesh (octree, one-ring lists, boundary flags, partial normals). A render binding copies proxy positions back into the untouched render mesh, so UVs, materials, textures and hard edges survive.
- interaction/input: existing MediaPipe hands and head tracking, pinch = pen down.
- voice: existing ElevenLabs Scribe/TTS plus the command grammar.
- undo.js: one timeline for strokes, part ops and Fable builds.
- scene/sync.js: sends HOLOEDIT packets to the server.

2) NODE SERVER (Node 24, server.js):
- server/blender-process.js owns exactly one headless Blender: spawn, token, HOLO_READY, stdin-EOF life-link, backoff restart, autosave reopen, warm-up.
- server/blender.js: the Fable 5.1 build loop. runBuild is kept, with a new SYSTEM prompt, look_web, and preview/model SSE.
- server/scene.js: working state {rev, parts, hashes, building}, persisted to HOLOMODEL_HOME/working; routes /api/scene*, /api/build.
- versions.js/history.js: GLB + .blend + thumbnail per version in the MongoDB Atlas GridFS 'snapshots' bucket, with local fallback.
- voice.js (ElevenLabs) and instrument.js (Sentry) unchanged apart from keyterms.

3) HEADLESS BLENDER 5.2.1: `blender -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 3 --python blender/headless.py -- <repo>/blender`. It runs the bridge add-on plus a new webio.py: export_glb, apply_web_edits, look_web, audit, densify/remesh/add_primitive/set_material, clear_scene, save_working. No GUI Blender ever.

SOURCE OF TRUTH
- Blender's .blend is the parametric truth. Fable's modifier stacks and procedural node trees survive on every part the user never sculpted.
- The page holds a live, editable copy.
- Web->Blender: HOLOEDIT packets (full welded mesh on first sculpt or after a topology change, positions-only by _vid afterwards, plus transforms/delete/dup). They are always flushed before any server operation (Fable build, version save/restore, detail op, export).
- Blender->web: non-destructive GLB exports. The page swaps only parts whose geometry hash changed, so untouched sculpted parts keep their proxy and undo history.
- Editing is paused (view gestures still work) while Fable builds, so the two sides can't conflict.

UNITS AND FRAMES
- Blender: metres, Z up, front -Y.
- GLB: metres, Y up. Blender (x,y,z) -> glTF (x,z,-y); the reverse is (x,-z,y). Quaternion glTF [x,y,z,w] -> Blender (w,x,-z,y); scale (sx,sy,sz) -> (sx,sz,sy).
- The web keeps the glTF root untouched in metres under a display parent (x100 to cm x fit x place x rotY). Brush radius is set in box-cm and converted per dab to part-local metres.
- Identity is always userData.holo_id (glTF extras), never names: three renames "Teapot Body" to "Teapot_Body" and "Cube.001" to "Cube001".

DEVELOPMENT RULES FOR THE EXECUTING AGENT
- Work on a branch (v3-headless-sculpt). Run the dev server with PORT=8766 so the user's instance on 8765 is left alone.
- Only headless Blender (-b --factory-startup), never a GUI.
- Commit per milestone only if the user OKs it.
- Reusable prototypes live in scratchpad plan/: recipe.py, srv/{manager.mjs,pump.py,proto_cmds.py,webedit.mjs}, parity/{blender_ref.py,port_check2.mjs,ref/*.json}, proto/{index.html,vendor/*}, webmap/{weldmap.mjs,seamy.glb,teapot_uv.glb}, blender_sculpt_presets.json.
plan.data_flow:
BOOT
1. npm start. blender-process.js spawns headless Blender with windowsHide, env HOLO_BRIDGE_TOKEN=crypto.randomBytes(16) (never in argv), HOLO_BRIDGE_PORT=0 and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, then waits for the 'HOLO_READY {port,pid}' line (measured 1.85-1.91 s).
2. It reopens HOLOMODEL_HOME/working/current.blend if present.
3. Warm-up: one throwaway glTF export (the first export pays ~340-500 ms of module import) and one tiny EEVEE render (the first pays ~0.9 s of shader compile).
4. The page loads GET /api/scene -> {rev, glbUrl, parts[{id,name,tris,sculpted,textured,ghash,mhash}], sym, building}, then loads the GLB. Proxies are built in idle time, largest part first (21.7 ms for the teapot body, roughly 0.2-0.5 s for 150-400k tris).

MAKE ("make a victorian teapot")
1. Scribe -> commands.js finds no local command -> scene/build.js POST /api/build {mode:'make', prompt} (SSE).
2. The server flushes nothing (make starts fresh), saves the current scene as a version if its fingerprint changed, then runs clear_scene.
3. runBuild runs Fable with run_blender_python, look_at_model (= look_web), web_search, web_fetch and generate_texture.
4. After each successful exec: export_glb mode=preview (no densify, no bake; 53-80 ms warm on the teapot), rev++, SSE {type:'preview', rev, url, tris}. The page shows it as a ghost and pauses editing; view gestures still work.
5. look_web renders an export in mode=look (final geometry density, 256 px bakes) inside a temp scene: import 0.127 s, 2 views at 768 px in about 1.1 s. Fable judges exactly the density the user will sculpt.
6. On done: export_glb mode=final (densify + 1024 px EMIT bakes), snapshot the .blend (23-44 ms), Workbench 256 px thumbnail (80-100 ms), versions.add({glb, blend}, thumb) to GridFS. SSE {type:'model', rev, url, version}.
7. The page runs load.js, keeps the placement, pushes an undo entry {fable, before: in-memory previous part set, versionBefore}.

CHANGE BY VOICE ("make the lid gold", often while pointing)
1. The page ends any stroke and awaits sync.flush(). Blender now holds every hand edit and autosaves.
2. POST /api/build {mode:'change', prompt, focus:{holo_id,name} from the 1.5 s THAT_MS pointing memory}.
3. The server snapshots pre-build.blend and checkpoints a version if the fingerprint changed. Fable's user message gets the part list with tris and holo_sculpted flags plus: "keep sculpted shapes; preserve holo_id; focus part = X".
4. Previews stream in as in MAKE, with editing paused.
5. On model, the page compares hashes per part:
   - same ghash and mhash: keep the live part (proxy, octree, undo history);
   - mhash only changed: swap materials, keep the proxy;
   - ghash changed: replace the part (its stroke undo entries fold into the fable entry);
   - new ids: add them; missing ids: remove them.
6. Cancel: if an exec is running, the server kills Blender, respawns it (~2.8 s) and reopens pre-build.blend. The page never changed, so nothing is lost.

HAND EDIT (main loop)
1. Each frame the ray runs from input.eye through the index fingertip.
2. Hover picks with the part's proxy octree (plain three Raycaster until the proxy exists), and the brush ring is drawn on the hit area normal.
3. Pinch (on below 0.28, off above 0.45; 400 ms aim memory): the stroke locks to the part under the ray, like Blender's active object.
4. stroke.js walks from the last dab to the new sample at spacing% of the diameter in world units, with a time-normalised lazy mouse. Each dab raycasts the stroke-start surface. Pressure is p=1 unless 'pressure on'.
5. cache.js computes radius, bstrength, area normal/centre and brush plane. The symmetry passes route mirrored dabs.
6. factors.js computes weights, the kernel moves proxy vertices, then auto-smooth runs.
7. binding.js scatters positions and normals to the render copies and uploads only dirty ranges (addUpdateRange).
8. Dab time budget is 6 ms per frame. Over budget, that frame's spacing widens and the overlap factor is recomputed, so total deposit stays the same.
9. Pen up (release-flick guard: dabs only while pinchRatio < 0.30; the end point is taken from about 100 ms before release): undo entry {part, idx, before, after}, part.dirty.mesh = true.
10. Within 600 ms of a second hand appearing, the stroke is cancelled and restored.
11. sync.flush() runs 1.5 s after the last edit, and always before build, version, restore, detail op or export. It POSTs /api/scene/edits?base=rev with a raw HOLOEDIT body (readRaw, 64 MB limit; readJson caps at 256 KB).
12. The server writes working/edits/<rev>.bin. The bridge runs apply_web_edits: numpy read, mesh/verts/xform/delete/dup ops, then save_working. Reply {rev, parts:{id:{ghash,mhash,nv}}}.
13. A 409 (base mismatch) reloads /api/scene. This should never happen, because editing is paused during builds.

QUICK OPS (no Fable)
- hide/isolate/show all, focus, delete, duplicate: local, then synced as ops.
- add primitive: POST /api/scene/command {op:'add_primitive'}. Blender adds the primitive, exports that one part (~50 ms) and the page inserts it.
- 'add detail': instant in-browser subdivision on welded edges, synced as a mesh op.
- 'smooth subdivide' and 'remesh': Blender ops on one part (~1 s), then a one-part swap.
- Recolour, shiny, metal: go to Fable by default (see decision 2). 'quick <colour>' does a local material-clone change synced with set_material.

UNDO/REDO (public/js/undo.js, 64 entries or 256 MB)
- Entries: stroke {part, idx, before, after}, xform, material, delete/dup/add, detail {part, old geometry}, fable {prevParts in memory (last 5), versionBefore}.
- Undoing a stroke restores positions, refreshes touched normals and octree boxes, and marks the part dirty (the next flush writes it into Blender).
- Undoing a Fable build swaps the in-memory part set instantly and asks the server to restore versionBefore's .blend in the background.

VERSIONS
- Automatic after every Fable build.
- 'save version': flush, snapshot, export_glb final, canvas.toBlob thumbnail -> GridFS {blendFileId, glbFileId} (local ${id}.blend/.glb fallback).
- 'go back to version N': flush, checkpoint current, then GET /api/history/:id/model.glb loads in the page at once while the bridge restores the .blend.
- state.json persists the current version and rev across server restarts. Versions are pruned to about 40 (Atlas M0 is 512 MB).

EXPORT
'export': flush, then download GET /api/scene/:rev.glb. That is Blender's own final GLB (sculpts plus Fable's materials), and the .blend is offered as a second download.
plan.export_recipe:
All numbers below were measured headless in Blender 5.2.1 (-b --factory-startup) on this laptop (Core Ultra 7 255H, Intel Arc 140T).

A) BLENDER -> WEB: bridge command export_glb {path, mode:'preview'|'look'|'final', only?:[holo_id]}
It never changes the scene: every temporary change is undone in a finally block.

1. Export set: objects where visible_get() and not hide_render and not name.startswith('_holo'). Select exactly these and export with use_selection=True, so the GLB and Fable's renders always contain the same objects. (hide_set objects were left out of the GLB but still rendered; hide_render-only objects were exported.) headless.py deletes the factory Cube, camera and light at start: the Cube cost Fable a whole turn in the teapot build and leaked into its GLB.

2. ensure_ids: every object gets o['holo_id'] (uuid4 hex[:12]) if it is missing or duplicated by obj.copy(), and o['holo_name'] = o.name. The fingerprint ignores custom props, so this never dirties versions.

3. Temporary modifiers, all removed afterwards:
   a) '_holo_realize' Realize Instances node-group modifier on geometry-nodes objects. Without it GN instances are dropped with a warning, and convert(target='MESH') gives 0 verts.
   b) look/final modes: Subsurf levels = render_levels (teapot: 31,808 -> 126,272 tris, 578 KB -> 2.28 MB, 167 ms).
   c) look/final modes: a SIMPLE Subdivision '_holo_dense' on unsculpted parts whose mean evaluated edge length is above 0.004 x model diagonal, with levels = min(4, ceil(log2(meanEdge / (0.004*diag)))). Caps: 150k tris per part, 400k total. Never applied to holo_sculpted parts, which are already at web density.
   Metaballs never export (the prompt forbids them and audit reports them).

4. Sculpt ids: only for parts with no modifiers (holo_sculpted, or plain meshes), add an INT point attribute '_vid' = range(n) and set o['holo_nv'] = n, o['holo_vidok'] = True. It exports as _VID FLOAT, and three loads it as geometry.attributes._vid. For a smooth mesh with no UVs, glTF order equals Blender order exactly.

5. Hints stored as extras:
   - scene['holo_sym']: Mirror-modifier axes merged with a KDTree self-match of evaluated verts across the root's X and Y planes (0.5% of diagonal threshold), in three axes (Blender X -> X, Y -> Z, Z -> Y). The teapot mirrors on Blender Y, which is three Z.
   - Per object: holo_ghash (sha1 of numpy foreach_get evaluated positions + matrix_world) and holo_mhash (material node values).
   - scene['holo_rev'] = rev, scene['holo_units'] = 'm'.

6. Procedural bake (final at 1024 px, look at 256 px, preview none):
   - Detect Principled inputs (Base Color, Roughness, Metallic, Emission Color, Alpha) fed by anything other than an Image Texture (optionally through a Normal Map node).
   - UVs: smart_project(angle_limit=1.15192) only on meshes with no UV map, run in edit mode on all objects sharing a material together (one atlas; 5-22 ms). Running it on meshes that already have UVs would destroy them.
   - EMIT trick: a temporary Emission node fed from the input's upstream socket into Material Output, bake type EMIT. Colour images are sRGB; roughness and metallic images are Non-Color.
   - Settings: Cycles, device CPU (the Arc oneAPI device takes 12.9 s on its first bake and is slower after), samples 1, margin 8.
   - Accuracy: EMIT gives 0.486/0.737/0.906 against the expected 0.484/0.735/0.906. A DIFFUSE/COLOR bake gives 0.475/0.722/0.890 and scales by (1 - metallic).
   - Timings: 512 px ~105 ms, 1024 px 320-380 ms, 2048 px 1.5 s, teapot 5-object atlas at 1024 px 778 ms, EMIT at 256 px 7-11 ms.
   - Cache by (mhash, mesh hash). Pack the images, wire them into the BSDF for the export, then restore the procedural links, selection, render engine and samples.

7. The exact call:
   bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(filepath=p, export_format='GLB', use_selection=True, use_visible=True, use_renderable=True, export_apply=True, export_yup=True, export_extras=True, export_attributes=True, export_materials='EXPORT', export_image_format=('JPEG' if no alpha and no normal map else 'AUTO'), export_draco_mesh_compression_enable=False, export_animations=False, export_cameras=False, export_lights=False)
   - Never use Draco or meshopt: Draco quantises to 14 bits and reorders vertices, which breaks sculpt round trips.
   - The defaults are silently wrong: export_apply=False and use_visible=False gave 3,980 tris, dropped the Mirror halves and included the hidden Cube.

8. Measured results:
   - Teapot, apply + visible: 578,616 B, 31,808 tris, 15,988 verts, 30-80 ms warm.
   - Scaling: 82k tris 1.5 MB / 80 ms; 328k tris 7.5-9.9 MB / 370-738 ms; 1.31M tris 30 MB / 1.24 s.
   - Images: a 1024 px colour map is 42 KB as JPEG against 339 KB as PNG.
   - Web load: three r170 GLTFLoader parses 578 KB in 5.8 ms and a 12.9 MB / 504k-tri file in 19 ms.
   - Survives: base colour, metallic and roughness factors; Coat (KHR_materials_clearcoat, loads as MeshPhysicalMaterial); Transmission; Sheen; Emission + strength; Alpha (BLEND); packed image textures on a real UV map; Color Attribute (COLOR_0); bevelled curves and text as meshes; parent TRS; custom props as extras/userData.
   - Lost: Subsurface; Bump; Glass BSDF (renders white); unbaked procedurals (white); image texture without a UV map (texCoord -1, invalid glTF). These are reported by audit and fed back to Fable.

B) WEB -> BLENDER: bridge command apply_web_edits {path}
The HOLOEDIT packet is [u32 LE headerLen][UTF-8 JSON header][pad to 4][binary blobs]. The header is {base, ops:[...]}; each blob is referenced as [byteOffset, count]. Blender reads it with numpy.frombuffer. All positions are glTF node-local metres; the page un-bakes any non-uniform scale first.

Ops:
- mesh {id, name?, nv, nt, pos Float32 nv*3, tri Uint32 nt*3, mat Uint8/Uint16 nt, uv Float32 nt*3*2 corner UVs (v flipped: 1-v) | null, sharp Uint32 vertex pairs | null}
  - Build with foreach_set in exactly the proxy's vertex order. There is no remove_doubles, because the page already welded.
  - Positions (x,y,z) -> (x,-z,y). Per-polygon material_index (recipe.replace_mesh only kept slot 0: fix this). UV layer, 'sharp_edge' attribute, shade_smooth.
  - Keep the object's material slots, run modifiers.clear() (the page edited the evaluated shape), then set _vid = range(nv), holo_nv, holo_vidok and holo_sculpted.
  - Timings: 20 ms (replace_mesh 20.3 ms; build 18.7 ms + weld 11.4 ms in the older variant).
  - An unknown id creates a new object under the root.
- verts {id, nv, pos}: check holo_vidok and holo_nv == len(vertices), otherwise error 'resend as mesh'. Then co[vid] = (x,-z,y) with numpy foreach_set: 4.5 ms for 8,258 verts, 24.5 ms for 164k.
- xform {id, t, r, s}: root-relative glTF TRS -> Blender loc (x,-z,y), quat (w,x,-z,y), scale (sx,sz,sy), applied through the parent.
- delete {id}
- dup {src, id, t, r, s}: obj.copy() + data.copy(), which keeps modifiers.
- set_material {id, color, roughness, metallic}: only for the optional quick-edit path.

Afterwards: undo_push, save_working (compressed .blend, 23-44 ms, images packed first), and a reply {parts:{id:{ghash,mhash,nv}}}. The whole thing is one bridge call, measured at 49-103 ms for the teapot prototype.

Do NOT use GLTFExporter -> import_scene.gltf as the sync channel. It renames _vid to __VID, merge_vertices reorders vertices (3 of 4,162 kept their index), and it adds custom split normals, QUATERNION rotation and '.001' duplicate materials.

C) OTHER BLENDER TIMINGS TO DESIGN AROUND
- Cold spawn: HOLO_READY at 1.85-1.91 s; Python is ready 1.8 s after launch.
- Kill -> restart: 2.84 s.
- Memory: idle 190 MB; 570-670 MB after the first EEVEE render; 1.4 GB holding 1.3M tris.
- Renders: EEVEE 512 px 16 spp 1.29 s first, then 0.43 s; Workbench 80-100 ms; Cycles CPU 16 spp 0.28 s (1.9 s with OIDN).
- Snapshot: 23-44 ms (teapot .blend 140 KB).
- The recorded teapot build took 7 turns, $1.35 and 235 s.
plan.sculpt_plan:
GOAL
Sculpting must feel like Blender's sculpt mode, driven by hands and voice.

Why not use an existing engine: no open-source web engine is 1:1 with Blender.
- three r186 Sculptor and SculptGL both use a 3d^4-4d^3+1 falloff, a Smooth with no falloff, and no strength^2, hardness, presets, overlap normalisation, lazy mouse, Clay Strips, Layer, Plane, Thumb, Nudge or Elastic.
- Sculptor also has no undo, symmetry, mask or pressure, and it drops UVs and material groups.

So we take mesh infrastructure from MIT code and behaviour from Blender itself, and prove the behaviour with automated parity tests against real Blender.

1. ENGINE AND THREE.JS INTEGRATION

Proxy mesh: public/js/sculpt/vendor/SculptorMesh.js + SculptorUtils.js (MIT, copied from scratchpad plan/proto/vendor, three r186, header 'adapted from SculptGL'; keep LICENSE-SculptGL.txt).
- Used as-is: the octree (collectIntersectRay, collectIntersectSphere), getVerticesRingVert/RingFace, getVerticesOnEdge (boundary), face and vertex normals, face boxes, tag/sculpt flags.
- Our fork adds:
  - initFromWelded(positions, triangles, triRenderMap): no position re-weld; proxy vertex i = Blender _vid i when _vid exists.
  - Float32 mask[] per vertex.
  - Lazy per-vertex stroke-start arrays origP/origN, keyed by the sculpt flag.
  - Per-face material id.
- Sculptor.js and SculptorTools.js are NOT imported (pointer code and non-Blender kernels). Their split/collapse becomes topology.js only in the dyntopo stretch.

Welding and render binding: binding.js.
- Weld render vertices by _vid when present, else by quantised position (1e-6 m) within a part only. Proven: 9,610 -> 8,258 verts in 11 ms, 0.0000 cm crack after 5 smooth passes across a material border.
- Multi-material Groups are merged first (mergeGeometries(geos, true), missing attributes filled), so one Blender object = one part = one proxy.
- CSR map: proxy vertex -> render copies. Proxy triangles map to render triangles; degenerate ones are dropped only from the proxy.
- Normal groups (proxy id + quantised exported normal):
  - UV-seam copies share the welded normal. This fixes the measured seam-normal dot product of 0.72 down to -0.84.
  - Hard-edge copies recompute from their own render faces, so flat parts stay flat.
- After each frame's dabs: scatter touched positions and normals, addUpdateRange on position and normal, needsUpdate. frustumCulled = false while stroking; bounds are recomputed at stroke end. UVs, textures and materials stay on the untouched render geometry, and textures stretch like in Blender.
- Non-uniform node scale is baked into the geometry at load (with a stored bake matrix that sync inverts).
- Proxies are built at idle right after load, largest first. The stroke locks to one part, like Blender's active object.

2. BLENDER LAYER (GPL-3.0-or-later)
Every file carries an SPDX header naming its source file at blender@235621e (plan/blender-src). It is paraphrased from the maths, not transliterated.

stroke.js (paint_stroke.cc)
- First dab at stroke start. Step = spacing% x diameter in WORLD units (Blender's scene-spacing mode) along the hand path.
- Each step interpolates the eye ray and raycasts the part's stroke-start surface.
- Overlap factor = 1/max of the summed falloff at 10 offsets (only with use_space_attenuation and spacing < 100).
- Pressure is lerped between samples.
- Lazy mouse on the 3D aim point:
  - ignore samples within 0.3 cm;
  - else move toward the sample by 1 - 0.9^(dt/8.33 ms), i.e. Blender's 0.9-per-event normalised to time, so 30 Hz webcam input doesn't lag;
  - off for Grab, Elastic, Snake Hook, Thumb, Rotate and Pose, as in Blender.
- Skip the first dab for brushes that need a stroke direction (Clay Strips, Plane family, Pinch, Clay Thumb).
- Grab family: restore the mesh to stroke start every step and apply the total delta.
- 6 ms per-frame dab budget. Over budget, widen spacing for that frame and recompute the overlap factor.

cache.js (sculpt.cc)
- Radius: box-cm -> part-local metres per dab.
- bstrength table, with a = S^2:
  - Draw/Draw Sharp/Layer/Crease/Blob: a*flip*p*ov
  - Clay: 0.25*a*flip*p^4*(1+ov)/2
  - Clay Strips: 0.3*a*flip*p^1.5*ov
  - Clay Thumb: 1.3*a*p^2*ov
  - Inflate: 0.25*a*flip*p*ov (0.125 when deflating)
  - Pinch: a*flip*p*ov (0.25x when magnifying)
  - Plane: a*p*(1+ov)/2 (0.5*a*p*ov when inverted in invert-displacement mode)
  - Smooth: flip*a*p
  - Nudge: a*p*(1+ov)/2
  - Thumb/Rotate: a*p
  - Grab/Snake Hook/Elastic/Pose: S (not squared, no pressure)
  - Mask: a*flip*p*(1+ov)/2
- Area normal and centre: smoothstep weights 3q^2-2q^3 (q = 1-d/R) over normal_radius_factor*r (area_radius_factor for Plane). Front and back sets are accumulated separately, front preferred. Centre = mean(L + (P-L)(1-w)).
- ACCUMULATE-OFF RULE (Blender default, written down because it moved parity from 4.1% to 1.5%): dab raycast, area normal/centre and Inflate vertex normals all read the stroke-start data.
- Brush plane on the main symmetry pass only, with plane_offset and Plane's stabilize_normal/plane averaged over up to 20 frames.
- Grab delta and stroke direction.

symmetry.js (mesh_paint.cc:388-424)
- Runs every subset of the enabled axes, including the identity.
- Mirroring is in the model-root frame about holo_sym's plane. For a single object that equals Blender's object space.
- The mirrored dab applies to the stroke part if it is self-symmetric; otherwise it goes to the part whose surface lies within 0.5r of the mirrored point (octree sphere query), so separate left and right parts work.
- The main pass's area normal and plane are reused mirrored, never recomputed. No centre-line skip (today's sculpt.js:38 skips within 0.3r); X movement cancels on the plane.
- The default axis comes from export hints and is announced by voice ("mirror Z on"). Radial symmetry is a stretch goal.

smooth.js (smooth.cc, sculpt_smooth.cc, enhance_details.cc)
- floor(4s) full passes plus one pass at 4s - floor(4s).
- Neighbour average: boundary vertices use only boundary neighbours; corners (2 boundary neighbours) stay fixed.
- Inverted = Enhance Details: per-stroke dir = avg - P, then push away.
- Also used for auto-smooth: after every dab of any brush except Smooth and Mask with autosmooth > 0 (Clay 0.25), at strength autosmooth x p.
- Also used for mesh filters.

3. BRUSH BUILD ORDER
Source in brackets: plan/blender-src/brushes/*.cc unless noted. Parity fixture in parentheses.

M2, core brushes:
1. Draw [draw.cc]: P += n*r*bstr*f, n = area normal over 0.5r (draw, draw_half_pressure, draw_mirror_x)
2. Smooth + Enhance [smooth.cc, sculpt_smooth.cc, enhance_details.cc] (smooth)
3. Grab [grab.cc]: P = origP + g*S*f(orig); g = 3D pinch delta in part space; optional silhouette (grab)
4. Inflate/Deflate [inflate.cc]: along stroke-start vertex normals (inflate)

M3, the rest of Tier 1 and Tier 2:
5. Clay Strips [clay_strips.cc]: brush-local box, zFactor = max(0, z(1-z)), square tip with tip_roundness, SMOOTHER falloff (clay_strips)
6. Plane family [plane.cc]: Flatten/Contrast, Scrape/Fill, Fill/Deepen, Plateau and Trim as presets of one height/depth kernel (flatten, scrape, fill)
7. Clay [clay.cc]: pull toward a plane 0.4r above the cursor (clay)
8. Snake Hook / Pull [snake_hook.cc]: location follows the hand, rake via quaternion^f, optional pinch (snake_hook)
9. Elastic Grab [elastic_deform.cc + bke/kelvinlet.cc]: regularised Kelvinlet triscale, eps = r, 2r, 4r, force bstr*20, nu = 0.4, all vertices. The most forgiving pull for hands. (elastic_grab)
10. Crease Polish/Sharp + Blob [crease.cc]: pinch strength = |bstr|*k^2/S^2, component along n removed (crease_sharp, blob)
11. Pinch/Magnify [pinch.cc] (pinch)
12. Layer [layer.cc]: D += f*bstr*(1.05-|D|), target = origP + origN*height*D; plateaus at exactly height (layer: Blender gives 0.05000)
13. Mask [mask.cc]: add f*bstr*(1-m) or erase f*bstr*m. Ops clear/invert/grow/shrink/blur adapted from SculptGL Masking.js (MIT). (mask)
14. If M3 is on schedule, otherwise M7: Nudge [draw.cc] (nudge), Thumb [thumb.cc] (thumb), Draw Sharp [draw_sharp.cc, POW4, original data] (draw_sharp)

Stretch: Clay Thumb [clay_thumb.cc], Rotate/Twist [rotate.cc, sign table {1,-1,-1,1,-1,1,1,-1}], Pose [sculpt_pose.cc, 4-6 h], Relax/Slide [relax.cc, topology_slide.cc], Multiplane Scrape.

Skipped: Cloth, Boundary, multires, texture/colour paint, trim/lasso gestures, face-set tools, curves sculpting.

4. HAND AND VOICE MAPPING
- Pen down: the existing pinch hysteresis (0.28 on / 0.45 off), 400 ms aim memory, 600 ms two-hand takeover cancel.
- Release-flick guard: dabs only while pinchRatio < 0.30, and the stroke end uses the tip from about 100 ms before release (150 ms ring buffer).
- Dab brushes use the eye -> fingertip ray.
- Grab family uses the 3D pinch-point delta through inverse(root.matrixWorld x part.matrix), with the existing depth gains.
- Pressure: default p = 1, exactly Blender with a mouse, which keeps Blender's formulas and parity intact.
  - 'pressure on': p_h = One-Euro(1.0, 0.05) of smoothstep((0.28 - pinchRatio)/0.20), mapped to [0.5, 1], multiplied after the Blender strength, so a half pinch never deposits nothing (Clay's p^4 would).
  - Mouse dev mode feeds PointerEvent.pressure from a Windows Ink pen into Blender's real curves, for a noise-free feel comparison.
- Modifiers: 'invert'/'dig' = Ctrl; 'smooth' toggles; second-hand fist = temporary Smooth (Blender's Shift, GestureRecognizer, M6).
- Voice (commands.js BRUSHES remapped to preset keys):
  - brush names
  - bigger/smaller, brush size N
  - stronger/softer (+/-0.1 UI strength)
  - invert/normal, falloff smooth/sharp/constant..., harder/softer, auto smooth N
  - mirror on/off/x/y/z
  - pressure on/off, stabilise more/less
  - mask clear/invert/grow/blur
  - smooth/inflate/sharpen it all
  - add detail, smooth subdivide, remesh
  - clay view, hide/isolate/show all, focus on X
  - undo/redo
  - The HUD shows brush, radius, strength, falloff, symmetry and pressure; handviz draws the ring on the area normal plus symmetry ghost rings.

5. DETAIL STRATEGY (Blender's routes, no dyntopo port)
a) Parts arrive dense: export raises Subsurf to render levels plus a temporary SIMPLE subdivision (0.4% of diagonal, 150k/part, 400k total).
b) 'add detail': instant in-browser 1-level midpoint subdivision on welded edges. It keeps UVs, groups and hard edges (split corner UVs are interpolated per render triangle), refuses above 500k tris per part, rebuilds the proxy (undo stores the old geometry) and syncs as a mesh op.
c) 'smooth subdivide': Blender Catmull-Clark +1 on one part (keeps UVs), about 1 s, one-part swap.
d) 'remesh': Blender voxel remesh (voxel = r/8, preserve volume) on untextured parts only, refused on textured parts.
e) Stretch: constant-detail dyntopo from Sculptor's split/collapse on untextured single-material parts.
   - Split above maxLen, collapse below 0.4 maxLen, never coarser than the part's original mean edge. Sculptor's relative mode coarsened 1M to 801k.
   - Disabled for Grab, Rotate, Thumb, Layer, Draw Sharp, Elastic, Pose, Smooth and Mask, as in Blender.
   - 'Owned' render mode (the render geometry = proxy buffers), synced as mesh ops.

6. UNDO
Blender's model: the first touch of a vertex in a stroke saves its position and normal. That copy is both the brushes' original data and the undo record {part, idx Uint32, before Float32, after Float32}. Undo memory is proportional to what was touched: at most about 5.7 MB even for a 1M-tri part sculpted everywhere.
- Redo stack. One timeline with part ops and Fable entries; cap 64 entries or 256 MB.
- A brush exception cancels the stroke, restores the stroke-start snapshot and reports to Sentry.

7. PARITY TESTS (automated 1:1 proof, already working)
- scripts/blender-ref.py = plan/parity/blender_ref.py. It drives real Essentials brushes with bpy.ops.sculpt.brush_stroke headless. The tricks that make it work:
  - temp_override(window, VIEW_3D area, WINDOW region) on the factory layout (-b still has 1 window);
  - bpy.ops.ed.undo_push before mode_set (otherwise EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION);
  - override_location=True (otherwise every dab lands at the origin);
  - never call rv3d.update() (it crashes);
  - use_locked_size='SCENE' with unprojected_size = the DIAMETER (0.6 -> r 0.3).
- npm run parity:ref writes 21 cases (draw, draw_half_pressure, draw_mirror_x, inflate, smooth, grab, snake_hook, elastic_grab, clay, clay_strips, flatten, scrape, fill, layer, crease_sharp, blob, pinch, nudge, thumb, draw_sharp, mask) on a bumpy 2,562-vertex icosphere to test/fixtures/blender-ref (5.4 MB, gitignored, about 10 s).
- test/sculpt-parity.test.js replays with exec semantics:
  - one dab per recorded element, overlap factor 1 (paint_stroke.cc:939);
  - each dab's ray from ray_origin/ray_dir raycast on the stroke-start surface;
  - the case's brush settings, HAND_OVERRIDES off.
  It skips (not fails) when the fixtures are missing.
- Acceptance: max error at most 2% of Blender's max displacement for kernel brushes, and at most 5% for plane and area-centre brushes (clay, clay_strips, flatten, scrape, fill, snake_hook).
- Baseline already reached by the 60-line prototype: Draw 1.52%, half-pressure 1.44%, Inflate 1.40%.
- test/stroke.test.js checks spacing, overlap factor, lazy mouse and pressure interpolation against the paint_stroke.cc formulas, which exec replay doesn't exercise.
- Ground truth is the installed 5.2.1, not main.

9. PERFORMANCE TARGETS AND FALLBACK
- Stamp cost: Sculptor stamps measured 0.15-0.68 ms at 200k tris (Node), and 2.66 ms including the mirror pass on the teapot body in Edge.
- Target: 60 fps sculpting a 150k-tri Fable model with MediaPipe running (dab p95 is a Sentry metric).
- Fallbacks:
  - If the octree misbehaves, vendor three-mesh-bvh 0.9.15 (MIT, peer three >= 0.159) for picking.
  - If a proxy exceeds about 1M tris, swap in SculptGL's typed-array CSR rings (36 MB against 309 MB heap).
  - Move MediaPipe to a worker if frames exceed 16 ms.
web_features: GLB model from the hidden Blender. Parts are keyed by holo_id and labelled with the Blender name. Multi-material objects are merged into one part. Each part gets its own material clone. Non-uniform scale is baked in.

Rendering: RoomEnvironment PMREM, AgX tone mapping and sRGB output, so gold, metal and clearcoat look like Blender. Highlight is an overlay mesh, not emissive. A 'clay view' neutral matte toggle for reading form. A views[] render loop, ready for the Pepper's-ghost multi-view.
Head-tracked off-axis window, kept as is. Fit and placement, two-hand turn, resize and move, and voice spin all work on GLB models.
Point to pick a part (proxy octree raycast), 1.5 s 'that' memory, and a brush ring on the area normal with symmetry ghost rings.
Welded sculpt proxy per part. UV seams, material borders, hard edges and textures never crack or crease. Only touched ranges are uploaded.

Blender stroke engine: world-space spacing, overlap normalisation, time-normalised 3D lazy mouse, a skip-first-dab rule for brushes that need a direction, restore-each-step for the grab family, a 6 ms dab budget, a release-flick guard and a pen-up freeze.
Blender weight pipeline: squared strength with the per-brush multipliers, hardness, 10 falloff presets, front-face only, mask, island automask.

Brushes with Blender 5.2.1 Essentials defaults. M2: Draw, Smooth/Enhance, Grab, Inflate/Deflate. M3: Clay Strips, Flatten/Contrast, Scrape/Fill, Fill/Deepen, Plateau, Trim, Clay, Snake Hook/Pull, Elastic Grab, Crease Polish/Sharp, Blob, Pinch/Magnify, Layer, Mask. Also Nudge, Thumb and Draw Sharp if on schedule.
Auto-smooth after each dab. Symmetry X/Y/Z in the model frame, with the axis auto-detected and announced. Mirrored dabs are routed to the part under the mirrored point.
Mask operations (clear, invert, grow, shrink, blur) and mesh filters by voice (smooth/inflate/sharpen/scale it all), respecting the mask.
Per-stroke undo and redo on one timeline with moves, deletes, duplicates, detail ops and Fable builds. Undoing a Fable build swaps the scene back instantly from memory.
Pressure off by default (p=1, like a mouse). 'Pressure on' uses filtered pinch closeness in the 0.5-1 range. In mouse dev mode, Windows Ink pen pressure feeds Blender's real curves.
Voice control for every brush setting: brush by Blender name, bigger/smaller, stronger/softer, invert, falloff, hardness, auto smooth, mirror axes, pressure, stabiliser, and a HUD readout.
Fable build client: make and change, with the pointed part as focus, live preview ghosts, editing paused during builds, cancel, and a partial swap that keeps untouched sculpted parts live.

Sync of hand edits into Blender. A full welded mesh goes over on the first sculpt, positions only by _vid after that, plus transforms, delete and duplicate. Flushed before every build, save, restore, detail op and export.
Detail: dense parts on arrival, 'add detail' as an instant in-browser subdivision that keeps UVs, and 'smooth subdivide' and 'remesh' (untextured parts only) done in Blender in about 1 s.
Part operations: hide, isolate, show all, focus on a part, move a part, delete, duplicate, add primitive (made by Blender).

Versions strip in the workbench: auto-save after every build, 'save version' with a canvas thumbnail, 'go back to version N' loads the stored GLB instantly. GLB + .blend stored in MongoDB Atlas GridFS.

- export_glb in preview/look/final modes: ids, _vid, holo_sym (Mirror + KDTree), hashes, temporary realize and densify. Procedural bake waits until M5.
- /api/scene routes.
- load.js (flatten, merge, clones, display parent), parts.js.
- Env map + AgX, overlay highlight, octree/raycast hover, versions strip moved in.
- Demo: 'go back to version 4' loads the Fable teapot (history mu8q0i14-0fb874) out of the invisible Blender, lit like Blender's render, dense (126k tris), no default Cube. Point to highlight parts; two-hand turn and resize.
- Tests: test_bridge export cases pass; killing Blender restarts it in about 2.8 s; killing node makes Blender exit in about 100 ms.

M2 Sculpt core + Draw/Smooth/Grab/Inflate (5 h)
- SculptorMesh fork (initFromWelded, mask, origP/origN).
- binding.js (weld by _vid or position, normal groups, dirty-range scatter).
- stroke.js, cache.js with the accumulate-off rule, factors.js, symmetry.js, smooth.js with auto-smooth.
- undo.js stroke entries plus redo.
- Draw, Smooth/Enhance, Grab (3D delta), Inflate.
- Parity harness (scripts/blender-ref.py, test/sculpt-parity.test.js), weld and kernel tests.
- Demo: pinch-sculpt the teapot body with mirror on; teapot_uv.glb keeps seams and textures after heavy smoothing; 'undo', 'redo'.
- Tests: parity for draw, draw_half_pressure, draw_mirror_x, inflate, smooth and grab is at most 2%.
- Fallback if this slips past 7 h: ship Draw/Smooth/Grab only and move Inflate to M3.

M3 The Blender brush set + voice (5 h)
- Brushes: Clay Strips, Plane family (Flatten/Scrape/Fill/Plateau/Trim presets), Clay, Snake Hook/Pull, Elastic Grab, Crease/Blob, Pinch/Magnify, Layer, Mask plus mask ops. Nudge/Thumb/Draw Sharp if on schedule.
- Mesh filters, HAND_OVERRIDES, voice routing for every brush setting, HUD and ghost rings.
- Demo: 'clay strips', build a ridge, 'scrape', 'crease' a groove, 'mirror on', 'smooth it all', 'undo'.
- Tests: all implemented parity cases pass (at most 2% kernel, at most 5% plane/area-centre); Layer plateau 0.05.

M4 Round trip with Fable (4 h)
- HOLOEDIT sync.js and apply_web_edits (mesh then verts by _vid, xform/delete/dup), save_working, rev/409.
- SYSTEM and userMessage rewrite (headless-to-GLB, Principled only, 3-40 parts under one root Empty, 150k tris at viewport levels, holo_sculpted = keep shape, preserve holo_id, focus part).
- look_web on the look-mode export; preview/model SSE; editing paused during builds; partial swap by ghash/mhash.
- Cancel kills Blender and reopens pre-build.blend.
- Versions with GLB + .blend in GridFS; Fable undo entry with in-memory scenes.
- Demo: sculpt the spout, point at the lid and say 'make the lid gold with a pearl knob'. Only the lid changes and the sculpted spout stays live. 'undo' swaps back instantly. 'go back to version 5'.
- Tests: test_bridge round trip exact; kill Blender mid-session and the page keeps sculpting while sync retries.

M5 Detail and materials (2 h)
- In-browser 'add detail' subdivision (keeps UVs).
- Blender 'smooth subdivide' and 'remesh' (untextured only) with one-part swap.
- EMIT procedural bake in final export (1024 px, cached, JPEG), 256 px in look mode.
- Audit notes to Fable.
- Demo: a coarse part becomes carvable after 'add detail'; a procedural wood material appears correctly in the web.

M6 Hands and stage hardening (3 h)
- Hands: release-flick guard, pen-up freeze, pressure on/off plus Windows Ink pen, second-hand fist = temporary Smooth.
- Blender safety: sandbox file-write block.
- Performance: dab time-budget tuning at 400k tris with MediaPipe running, Sentry spans and dab p95.
- Demo prep: 2-3 prebuilt demo versions built the night before; rehearse the full script twice, including a forced Blender taskkill and a mouse-mode fallback run.
- Demo: the full script twice without a restart, with the Sentry dashboard live.

M7 Stretch (after the ~24 h core), roughly in this order:
- Nudge/Thumb/Draw Sharp if not done in M3.
- Constant-detail dyntopo on untextured parts (Sculptor split/collapse, owned mode).
- MediaPipe GestureRecognizer in a worker plus two-hand pitch.
- Radial symmetry, Clay Thumb, Rotate, Pose (4-6 h).
- Pepper's-ghost multi-view renderer on views[]; Kinect source writing into input/state.js.
risks_and_mitigations:
Hand input is much noisier than a mouse (palm-size depth jitter, pointing error magnified about 3.4x into the box, about 30 Hz samples), so Blender-accurate brushes can still feel shaky.
- Mitigations: One-Euro filtering, time-normalised 3D lazy mouse, world-space spacing, front-face only, release-flick guard plus pen-up freeze, Elastic Grab as the forgiving pull.
- Pressure is off by default, and a Windows Ink pen in mouse mode checks feel without webcam noise.

Parity has limits. The source is Blender main@235621e, but the ground truth is the installed 5.2.1, and Plane/Clay Strips were reworked recently. The exec replay tests kernels with overlap factor 1, not spacing or lazy-mouse feel.
- Mitigations: installed Blender is the reference (npm run parity:ref regenerates it); 5% tolerance for plane/area brushes; stroke.test.js pins the paint_stroke.cc formulas.

Main-thread contention: MediaPipe face and hand inference plus sculpting plus uploads.
- Mitigations: octree queries, touched-only normals, range uploads, a 6 ms dab budget that widens spacing with overlap renormalisation, the 150k Fable prompt budget and 400k export cap, and idle proxy builds.
- MediaPipe moves to a worker if frames exceed 16 ms.

Sculptor is two weeks old (a decimation bug and a wireframe-cache issue were mentioned in its PR).
- Mitigations: pinned vendored copy with a minimal fork; only its mesh and octree are used (no tools, no dyntopo in the core); weld and parity tests cover it.
- Plan B: three-mesh-bvh 0.9.15 for picking and SculptGL CSR rings for big parts.

A web/Blender divergence could silently lose a sculpt when Fable rebuilds.
- Mitigations: flush is mandatory before every build, save, restore, detail op and export; base-rev 409; editing paused during builds; verts ops check holo_vidok and holo_nv and fall back to a full mesh op; test_bridge round-trip tests; state.json persistence.

Sculpting a part clears its modifier stack in Blender and turns it into a triangle mesh, so Fable can't edit that part parametrically any more.
- Mitigations: only touched parts are affected, because the export is non-destructive for everything else; the SYSTEM prompt says holo_sculpted parts must keep their shape; version history keeps the parametric source.

Materials can silently turn white (procedural, Bump, Glass BSDF, image texture without UVs).
- Mitigations: EMIT bake at export, audit notes after every exec, Principled-only rule in the SYSTEM prompt, and look_web so Fable sees exactly the GLB.
- Normal-map baking is not measured and not planned.

Headless Blender can hang on Fable code (e.g. while True), and cancel used to release the lock while exec kept running.
- Mitigations: the Node timeout or cancel kills Blender, it restarts in about 2.8 s and reopens the autosave or pre-build .blend.
- The page keeps its own copy, and only idempotent commands are retried after ECONNRESET, never exec.

Security: unattended exec plus prompt-injectable web_fetch content could write files (GLB and PNG writes were reproduced from the sandbox).
- Mitigations: the sandbox blocks export/import/save/render-write operators, Image.save and filepath_raw; the token lives in env; the server binds 127.0.0.1.

Detail operations destroy UVs (voxel remesh, and dyntopo later).
- Mitigations: remesh is refused on textured parts; 'add detail' uses UV-keeping subdivision; dyntopo, when added, only runs on untextured single-material parts.

Live Fable builds are slow and cost money (teapot: 7 turns, $1.35, 235 s).
- Mitigations: prebuilt demo versions, live preview ghosts that show progress, and cancel restores cleanly.

Size and storage: 328k tris means a 7.5-9.9 MB GLB; 1.3M tris means 30 MB and 1.4 GB of Blender RAM; Atlas M0 holds about 100 versions at 3 MB.
- Mitigations: 150k prompt budget and 400k cap, JPEG baked maps, binary positions-only syncs, pruning to about 40 versions, and the working autosave kept on local disk.

Venue network failure.
- Mitigation: all three.js, MediaPipe wasm and model files are served from public/vendor. ElevenLabs, Fable and Atlas still need the network: browser speech and TTS fallbacks exist, local history storage is the fallback, and prebuilt versions cover the rest.

Licence: Blender-derived JS makes the sculpt module GPL-3.0-or-later.
- The repo must be public with source, and that module can never go closed-source. MIT notices must be kept.
- Decision 1 covers this.

Development collision with the user's running app (node on 8765).
- Mitigation: the executing agent uses PORT=8766 and never kills the user's server.
- Blender-process uses port 0 plus a token with no bridge.json, and --factory-startup, so it can't collide with a GUI Blender that has the add-on.

decisions_for_user.question: Porting Blender's brush code makes the sculpting part GPL-3.0, so the whole repo has to be public and GPL-licensed. Are you OK with that?
options: Yes: repo goes GPL-3.0 and public, with a full Blender brush port that is parity-tested (this plan)

No: stay non-GPL. Use only MIT engines (three.js Sculptor/SculptGL brushes) and tune them by comparing outputs against real Blender without reading its code. This is slower and noticeably less Blender-like (no Clay Strips/Layer/Plane family out of the box)
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Yes, go GPL-3.0 and public. It's the only way to get the Blender-exact feel you asked for. Your Blender add-on is already GPL, and hackathon repos are public anyway.

decisions_for_user.question: Should simple looks-only voice edits ('make it red', 'shiny', 'metal') go to Fable, or happen instantly in the app?
options: Always Fable: 1-4 minutes, and Fable can do it properly (textures, whole-object restyles)
Fable by default, and saying 'quick red' / 'quick metal' makes an instant local change that still gets saved into Blender
Instant local for plain colours and finishes; Fable only for textured parts or open-ended requests
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Fable by default plus the 'quick' keyword. It matches what you asked for (voice changes go to Fable), and you still have an instant option for a snappy demo moment.

decisions_for_user.question: Should 'add detail under the brush as you sculpt' (Blender's dyntopo) be built now or later?
options: Later (stretch): parts arrive dense, 'add detail' subdivides instantly in the app, and 'smooth subdivide' / 'remesh' run in the hidden Blender in about 1 s
Now, inside the brush milestone: constant-detail dyntopo on untextured parts. It costs about 4-6 h, which pushes several brushes (Crease, Pinch, Layer, Mask) to stretch
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Later. Dense-on-arrival plus instant 'add detail' covers the demo, and more Blender brushes are worth more to the 'feels like Blender' goal than live detail.

scores.name: web-truth
scores.notes: Most robust architecture for a stage demo. Blender is stateless compute: a crash or cancel loses nothing, there is no continuous sync channel, no rev/409, and no stale _vid, and it can't disagree with the page. Its sculpting claim is the only one backed by evidence. I re-ran plan/parity/port_check2.mjs against the 21 golden Blender references in plan/parity/ref: Draw is 1.519%, half-pressure Draw 1.439% and Inflate 1.398% of Blender's max displacement, and Layer plateaus at exactly 0.0500. That makes '1:1 with Blender' a test that can be checked, not a promise. It builds on the Sculptor octree and split/collapse, already verified on r170 in Edge with the real teapot, instead of writing a new mesh substrate. It has the widest brush set, constant-detail dyntopo, part_op remesh/decimate/symmetrize and mask/filters, which is the best match for the user's core requirement. Weaknesses: (1) every Fable 'change' re-imports a triangulated, modifier-baked, texture-baked GLB into an empty scene. That happens even for parts the user never touched, so Fable's second and third edits work on steadily degraded source (Subsurf/Mirror/Solidify gone, procedural nodes now JPEGs, tris-to-quads heuristics). (2) Depends on the jsDelivr CDN. (3) About 29 h of milestones, with M3 fitting roughly 15 brushes into 6 h, so this is 'a day' only with ruthless tiering. (4) The multi-step import_web fix-up is its own fragile surface, though each fix-up has a test.

scores.name: blender-truth
scores.notes: Best at preserving Fable's work across iterations. The .blend stays authoritative, untouched parts keep live modifiers and procedural materials, and positions are written back by _vid in 4.5 to 24.5 ms. Its sculpt-engine thinking is the most faithful: pressure is off by default so it equals mouse Blender, it uses Blender's own pressure curves, and it adds a Windows Ink pen in mouse dev mode for a noise-free parity feel test. Downsides for the demo: it has the most moving parts on stage. That includes a debounced 800 ms flush and a binary container of verts/mesh/xform/dup/delete/add/apply_scale ops replayed as native bpy ops. Add to that holo_vidok and holo_nv staleness checks, rev/409 reloads, autosave reopen, and 'add a sphere' needing a Blender round trip plus a one-part export. If any piece misbehaves live, the headline promise (the sculpt survives 'make it gold') fails or forces a reload. Its parity plan hedges on whether headless brush_stroke can run, but it can: the golden references already exist. Its roughly 31 h of milestones, with sync alone at 5 h, is the least realistic for about a day.

scores.name: best-hybrid
scores.notes: Has the best demo-day instincts of the three. It vendors three, three-mesh-bvh and MediaPipe wasm plus models under public/vendor, so venue Wi-Fi can't kill it. It keeps prebuilt demo versions, because a live teapot build took 235 s and $1.35. Quick edits (recolour, shiny, metal, delete, duplicate, add) skip Fable's multi-minute latency. It rehearses a forced Blender crash, and a brush exception cancels and restores the stroke instead of throwing. On fidelity, it raises Subsurf to render levels and adds a SIMPLE densify on coarse parts at export, keeps parametric stacks on untouched parts, and uses a partial swap by holo_hash so untouched parts keep their undo and proxies. Its pressure design is clever: Blender's formulas run with p=1 and hand pressure is applied as a separate floored multiplier. Weaknesses: it writes a new mesh substrate from scratch (typed-array weld, CSR rings, normal groups, three-mesh-bvh shapecast collection and per-node refit, partial normals), which is not verified in the app, and demotes the Sculptor code that is already proven. Its '~19 h core' is not credible: M2 is 4.5 h for the substrate, stroke engine, factors, symmetry, undo and 4 brushes, and M3 is 3.5 h for about 12 brushes plus mask, filters, voice and HUD. It also states that numeric parity is not automatable because its explicit-location harness moved nothing. That is contradicted by plan/parity/ref, which has 21 working golden cases, so it would ship without the one test that proves the user's '1:1' requirement. It keeps continuous bidirectional sync (HOLOEDIT), with the same stage-fragility class as blender-truth, only somewhat smaller.

grafts: From best-hybrid, demo safety: vendor three@0.170 (plus GLTFLoader, GLTFExporter, BufferGeometryUtils, RoomEnvironment), three-mesh-bvh@0.9.15 and @mediapipe/tasks-vision 0.10.35 wasm with the face and hand .task models under public/vendor, and repoint the import map. Do this in the first hour so the demo never depends on the venue network or jsDelivr.

From best-hybrid: store 2-3 prebuilt Fable models as versions (the teapot mu8q0i14-0fb874 plus others built the night before). A live build is 1-4 min at about $1.35, so on stage open with 'go back to version N' and run the live Fable build in the background with previews streaming.

From best-hybrid, local quick edits that skip Fable: recolour, shiny/matte/metal, hide/isolate, delete, duplicate, add primitive. They apply to the page's per-part material clones and geometry at once. Web-truth's model is the source of truth, so they need no Blender call at all and simply ride along in the next change's GLB. Keep 'make the frame gold' routed to Fable when the material is textured or the phrasing is open-ended, as the user asked.

Hybrid of backend and blender-truth, fixing web-truth's main fidelity weakness. Store each Fable build's .blend alongside its GLB. On 'change', if the last build's .blend exists and the page's holo_ids match, open that .blend and apply the page's GLB by holo_id instead of importing into an empty scene. This is the apply_web_edits prototype in plan/srv/proto_cmds.py, already round-tripped in 49-103 ms. Replace meshes only for holo_edited=='mesh', transforms for moved parts, delete missing parts, add holo_new parts. Untouched parts keep their Subsurf/Mirror/Solidify stacks and procedural nodes. Fall back to web-truth's import_web when the .blend is missing or ids don't match. Blender stays stateless between requests, so crash safety is unchanged.

From best-hybrid: pass the pointed part (the existing THAT_MS 1.5 s memory) as focus {holo_id, name} in the Fable change request. After a build, swap only parts whose content hash changed, so untouched sculpted parts keep their live proxy, octree and per-stroke undo history.

From best-hybrid, pressure design: run Blender's per-brush strength formulas with p=1, which is exactly mouse Blender, then multiply by a separate One-Euro-filtered hand pressure floored at 0.5. This keeps the golden parity tests valid and keeps the formulas unmodified, instead of overriding Clay's p^4 and Clay Strips' p^1.5 to linear.

From best-hybrid: set the per-frame dab budget by time (about 6 ms) rather than a fixed count of 24. When over budget, widen that frame's spacing and recompute the overlap factor so the total deposit stays constant. A brush exception cancels the stroke, restores the stroke-start snapshot and reports to Sentry instead of killing the frame.

From best-hybrid: at final export, set Subsurf levels to render_levels and add a temporary SIMPLE subdivision on parts coarser than about 0.4% of the model diagonal, with 150k-per-part and 400k-total caps. Parts then arrive dense enough to sculpt without the user having to say 'add detail' first.

From blender-truth: a release-flick guard that emits dabs only while pinchRatio < 0.30, so opening the fingers never stamps. Also pen-pressure (PointerEvent.pressure from Windows Ink) in mouse dev mode, for a noise-free feel comparison against the user's own Blender.

From blender-truth: derive the symmetry default from Fable's Mirror-modifier axes (holo_sym, Blender Y maps to three's Z for the teapot) before falling back to the KDTree self-match. Announce the chosen axis by voice.

From blender-truth: an explicit 'owned' render mode for dyntopo parts, where the render geometry becomes Sculptor's growing buffers, so the proxy copy-back never tries to map through changed topology. Also blender-truth's full sandbox block list, and headless.py deleting the factory Cube, camera and light.

From best-hybrid: a views[] render loop in view.js from M1, so the Pepper's-ghost multi-view later is a config change. Also rehearse the full script twice, including a forced taskkill of Blender mid-session and a mouse-mode fallback run.
fatal_flaws: best-hybrid: says exact Blender parity 'is not automated yet' because its explicit-location harness moved nothing. That is false: plan/parity/ref already holds 21 golden headless brush_stroke cases, and port_check2.mjs reproduces Draw/Inflate within 1.4-1.52% (re-run in this review). Combined with writing the mesh substrate from scratch (weld, CSR, normal groups, BVH shapecast and refit) in a 4.5 h milestone and about 12 brushes plus mask, filters and voice in 3.5 h, its '~19 h core' is not credible. It would ship without the one test that proves the user's '1:1 with Blender' requirement.

blender-truth: continuous bidirectional sync is a live single point of failure for the core promise that sculpts survive voice changes. Its parts: an 800 ms debounced flush, a binary op container replayed as native bpy ops, _vid/holo_nv staleness, rev/409 reloads, and autosave reopen after a kill. Any glitch on stage either drops the sculpt when Fable rebuilds or 409s the page into a reload. Its ~31 h plan is also the furthest from 'about a day'.

web-truth (fatal only if left as is, fixed by the .blend-cache graft): every 'change' re-imports the whole model as a triangulated, modifier-baked, texture-baked GLB into an empty scene, including parts the user never touched. Fable's parametric source (Subsurf/Mirror/Solidify stacks, procedural node trees, quads) erodes with each voice edit, so the third 'make it X' works on baked triangle soup and Fable's detail degrades over a session.

scores.name: best-hybrid
scores.notes: Best balance of the three. Blender keeps the .blend as the source of truth and exports without changing the scene: modifiers are applied only in the export, and procedural materials are EMIT-baked and cached. Parts the user never touched therefore keep Fable's modifier stacks and node trees. Sculpted parts go back to Blender as raw welded arrays through a lifted replace_mesh (20 ms measured), not through the lossy GLTFExporter to import_scene.gltf path. The page swaps parts by holo_hash, so parts Fable did not change keep their live proxy, BVH and undo history. That is the most elegant answer to 'Fable changes the lid, my sculpted spout survives'. During export it sets Subsurf to render levels and adds a temporary SIMPLE subdivision to coarse parts, so the web gets the density Fable saw in its renders (teapot 31.8k to 126k triangles) and the parts are dense enough to sculpt. It has the most stage hardening: vendored three, three-mesh-bvh and MediaPipe; prebuilt demo versions; a rehearsed forced crash; the page keeps sculpting while Blender restarts; a 6 ms dab budget that widens spacing and recomputes the overlap factor so total deposit is unchanged. It passes Blender's formulas p=1 and applies hand pressure as a separate [0.5,1] multiplier, which keeps Blender's maths intact. Weaknesses: (1) It says numeric parity can't be automated. That is wrong: plan/parity has 21 golden cases that work (I re-ran port_check2.mjs; details under fatal flaws). Its own p6 harness moved nothing; I checked parity_hybrid/out and every file has moved 0. (2) It builds the SculptMesh (weld, CSR, normal groups, BVH gather and refit) from scratch in a 4.5 h M2, when Sculptor r186 is already verified in Edge on the teapot. (3) There is no in-browser dyntopo; 'add detail' and 'remesh' round-trip through Blender. (4) Quick recolour/shiny/metal skips Fable. That is good for latency but departs a little from the brief's 'voice changes go to Fable'. The core is about 19 h with a named fallback, the most believable schedule.

scores.name: web-truth
scores.notes: Strongest sculpting plan, and the only one that proves '1:1 with Blender'. Headless bpy.ops.sculpt.brush_stroke produced 21 golden reference cases. I confirmed the non-zero displacements: Layer plateaus at exactly 0.05000, Grab 0.68, Snake Hook 1.42. A JS Draw/Inflate port matches with accumulate-off semantics: Draw 1.52%, half pressure 1.44%, Inflate 1.40% of Blender's maximum displacement. It sets acceptance thresholds of 2% for kernel brushes and 5% for plane-based brushes. It also has the most editing features: the Sculptor r186 fork (verified in Edge) as the mesh layer plus three-mesh-bvh for hover, 19 brushes, constant-detail dyntopo on untextured parts, in-browser subdivision that keeps UVs, mask ops, filters, GestureRecognizer in a worker, second-hand fist as Smooth, and two-hand pitch. Mirrored dabs are sent to whichever part lies under the mirrored point, which handles separate left and right parts. Blender holds no state, so a crash or cancel loses nothing, and undoing a Fable change is an in-memory scene swap. The weakness is fidelity of the round trip. Every Fable change exports the page with GLTFExporter and runs import_scene.gltf(merge_vertices) into a fresh scene. The export investigator measured that path as lossy (vertex reorder, custom split normals, QUATERNION rotation, .001 materials, _vid renamed to __VID). It also throws away every part's modifier stack, the procedural node trees (already baked into JPEGs, which are then re-encoded on every round) and quads, including parts the user never touched. The plan's fix-ups cover these, but Fable's parametric source gets worse with every voice change. A new import-fix-up path on every change is also a single point of failure. The dependencies still load from the CDN. About 29 h plus 3 optional is ambitious for a hackathon.

scores.name: blender-truth
scores.notes: Most faithful round trip. Parts without modifiers get exact position writes by _vid (4.5 ms for 8k vertices, 24.5 ms for 164k with numpy), guarded by holo_nv and the export token. A part's first sculpt replaces its mesh once, in the proxy's vertex order, and from then on it takes cheap writes by _vid. Untouched parts keep their modifiers, and a dyntopo'd part gets a one-part re-bake of its procedural texture. A journal flush before every Fable build, restore or export, plus rev/409 checks and autosave, keeps Blender and the page consistent. Pressure is off by default (p=1), which makes plain mouse-driven Blender the honest 1:1 baseline, and it adds Windows Ink pen pressure in mouse mode. Sculptor is used only as the mesh layer, all brush behaviour is Blender-derived, and constant-detail dyntopo follows Blender's list of disallowed brushes. The cost is surface area. Sync has seven op types: verts, mesh, xform, delete, dup, add and apply_scale. Non-uniform scale is baked in the page and in Blender in lockstep, dyntopo parts switch to 'owned' geometry, and parts get re-baked individually. Any divergence silently corrupts the .blend that Fable edits next, and 'add a sphere' needs a Blender round trip. The parity test runs only 'if feasible', although web-truth showed it is. Dependencies stay on the CDN, and there is no three-mesh-bvh (hover uses a slow raycast until proxies are built). At about 31 h plus stretch goals it is the heaviest plan and the most likely to overrun.

grafts: From web-truth: adopt the parity harness that already works. Use plan/parity/blender_ref.py (temp_override on the factory VIEW_3D area, ed.undo_push before mode_set, override_location=True, no rv3d.update) and the 21 golden cases in plan/parity/ref as test/sculpt-parity.test.js. Replay with exec semantics (overlap factor 1, raycast and normals taken from the stroke-start surface) and set acceptance at 2% for kernel brushes and 5% for plane- and area-centre brushes. best-hybrid's claim that parity can't be automated is wrong: its own p6 harness moved nothing, while web-truth's harness gives Draw 1.52%, Inflate 1.40% and a Layer plateau of exactly 0.05. Add npm run parity:ref to regenerate the references against the installed 5.2.1.

From web-truth and blender-truth: build the proxy on the vendored, forked three r186 SculptorMesh instead of a from-scratch SculptMesh. It supplies the octree, one-ring neighbours, boundary flags, partial normals and updateRange uploads, and it is verified in Edge with r170 on the Fable teapot at 2.66 ms per stamp including the mirror pass. Add initFromWelded, a mask array, per-face material ids and undo hooks. Keep three-mesh-bvh only for hover picking across parts on the render meshes. This takes the biggest risk out of M2 and leaves room for constant-detail dyntopo later.

From blender-truth: once a part's mesh has been replaced (it now has no modifiers and has _vid = range(n) in proxy order), sync it as positions only by _vid, checked against holo_nv and the export token. Stop sending full triangles, UVs and material indices on every 1.5 s flush. Send the full topology only on the first sculpt or after a topology change.

From blender-truth: make pressure off (p=1) the default so that plain mouse-driven Blender is the 1:1 baseline, and turn best-hybrid's [0.5,1] hand-pressure multiplier on by voice. Keep Windows Ink PointerEvent.pressure in mouse dev mode for feel checks against Blender with a pen.

From web-truth: for symmetry, mirror the dab in the model-root frame and send it to whichever part lies under the mirrored point, so separate left and right parts (ears, handles) mirror correctly. Also detect symmetry with a KDTree self-match at export, not only from Mirror-modifier axes, because Fable often builds symmetric models without a Mirror modifier. Announce the detected axis by voice.

From web-truth: keep the last ~5 pre-change GLBs in memory, so undoing a Fable change is an instant scene swap. Restoring the .blend then happens in the background instead of blocking on a version-restore round trip.

From web-truth: move GestureRecognizer (landmarks plus Closed_Fist/Open_Palm) into a worker. A second-hand fist gives temporary Smooth (Blender's Shift), and two hands also control pitch. Use the in-browser simple subdivision that keeps UVs as an instant 'add detail' for textured parts. Add constant-detail dyntopo for untextured single-material parts: never collapse edges below the part's original mean edge length, which fixes Sculptor's relative mode that coarsened a 1M-triangle mesh to 801k.

From blender-truth: a release-flick guard that emits dabs only while pinchRatio < 0.30, alongside the 100 ms pen-up freeze. Also filter Blender 5.2's Material.use_nodes DeprecationWarnings out of the exec output Fable sees.

Consistency fix for best-hybrid itself: look_web should render a GLB with the same densify and render levels as the final export, or Fable judges a coarser mesh than the one the user sculpts. Also have Fable handle any colour change on a textured material or a part Fable owns ('make the frame gold'), so quick edits stay limited to trivial factors.
fatal_flaws: None of the three plans is fatally broken. The flaws below are the ones that would hurt most if left unfixed.

web-truth (serious fidelity flaw, not demo-fatal): every Fable change reimports the page's GLTFExporter output into a fresh Blender scene. That drops the modifier stacks, procedural node trees, quads and non-glTF material data of every part, including parts nobody touched, and re-encodes the baked JPEG textures each round. Fable's parametric detail gets worse with each voice change, and the import fix-up code sits on every change path.

best-hybrid: as written it ships with no numeric proof that sculpting matches Blender 1:1, because it wrongly concludes parity can't be automated. plan/parity already contradicts that. I re-ran port_check2.mjs: Draw has 1.52% error, half-pressure Draw 1.44% and Inflate 1.40%, with 21 non-zero golden cases. best-hybrid's own harness failed; every file in parity_hybrid/out shows moved 0. The fix is the parity graft.

best-hybrid: M2 gives 4.5 h to a from-scratch weld/CSR/normal-group/BVH-refit mesh core plus the stroke engine, the weight pipeline, symmetry, undo and four brushes. That is under-budgeted, and three-mesh-bvh has not been run in this app. Switch to the Sculptor fallback early, or better, graft SculptorMesh from the start.

blender-truth: the sync surface is large for a hackathon: verts by _vid, first-sculpt mesh replacement, apply_scale in lockstep, owned-mode dyntopo, per-part re-bake, and dup/add/delete ops, plus rev/409. It is the most likely plan to leave the .blend silently diverged from what the user sees, and at about 31 h it is the most likely to overrun.

scores.name: best-hybrid
scores.notes:
This is the strongest overall shape.
- Blender keeps the parametric .blend, so Fable's Subsurf, Mirror and Solidify stacks and its procedural materials survive on every part the user hasn't touched.
- The export is non-destructive, Subsurf is raised to render levels, and a temporary SIMPLE subdivision is added up to a density target. That matters most for Blender feel: brushes on the teapot body's 8k vertices look faceted, and on 30-100k they look like Blender.
- Hand edits go back as welded replace_mesh HOLOEDIT packets. That single sync path avoids the stale-_vid problems.
- A partial swap by holo_hash keeps the live proxy and undo history of untouched parts across Fable builds.
- The engine is its own CSR SculptMesh on three-mesh-bvh (shapecast plus partial refit), a proven fixed-topology pattern. It does not depend on internals of a two-week-old Sculptor, and Sculptor stays as a named fallback if M2 slips.
- Stage safety: dependencies are vendored (important on venue wifi), demo versions are prebuilt, a forced-crash rehearsal is planned, and the page keeps sculpting while Blender restarts.
- Weaknesses:
  - No in-browser dyntopo; detail comes from Blender subdivide or remesh in about 1 s.
  - Its claim that exact parity "is not automated yet" is wrong: the web-truth harness works. I reran it: Draw, half-pressure Draw and Inflate came out at 1.52%, 1.44% and 1.40% of Blender's max displacement, and all 21 references moved vertices, including Grab, Snake Hook and Elastic.
  - Lazy mouse at factor 0.5 departs from Blender's 0.9 but suits 30 Hz input.
  - The M2 (4.5 h) and M3 (3.5 h) estimates are optimistic, but the 19 h core leaves slack in a 36 h event.
  - Quick recolour that skips Fable slightly contradicts "voice changes go to Fable".

scores.name: web-truth
scores.notes:
This plan has the best sculpt evidence.
- blender_ref.py drives real Essentials brushes through headless brush_stroke. override_location=True and undo_push before mode_set are the key tricks. It writes 21 golden cases.
- I reproduced its JS port error: 1.52%, 1.44% and 1.40% with raycasts on the stroke-start surface (accumulate-off semantics) and 4.1% without. That is exactly the subtle behaviour a 1:1 port needs pinned down.
- It has the broadest editing set: constant-detail dyntopo on untextured parts, UV-keeping in-browser subdivision, 19 brushes, mask and filters, KDTree symmetry auto-detection, and a second-hand fist for Smooth.
- A stateless Blender is robust: a crash loses nothing, and undo across Fable changes is a scene swap in memory.
- The big cost is fidelity across iterations. Each change re-imports the web GLB, so every part loses its modifier stack, procedural materials become baked images, and quads become triangles (the tris-to-quads fix-up is a guess). Fable then works on dense triangle meshes it edits much worse, so "make the spout longer" degrades from build to build.
- It keeps viewport-level density, so it does not densify for sculpting.
- Dependencies stay on the CDN, which is a risk on venue wifi.
- 29 h of core milestones, with 15 brushes plus symmetry plus voice in 6 h, is tight.
- A Sculptor fork plus three-mesh-bvh means two spatial structures to maintain.

scores.name: blender-truth
scores.notes:
The architecture is sound: Blender stays the parametric truth, the export is non-destructive, and it has the most faithful hand choices.
- Pressure is off by default (p=1 is exactly Blender with a mouse), and when turned on it drives Blender's own per-brush curves.
- A Windows Ink pen in mouse mode lets you check brush feel against Blender with no hand noise.
- The release-flick guard only lays dabs while pinchRatio < 0.30.
- Radius is taken at stroke start, like view-locked, and switches to scene-locked for the hologram.
- It uses Blender's exact lazy stabiliser and exclusion list.
- Sync is the most complex of the three:
  - two write paths, positions by _vid for modifier-free parts and a one-time mesh replacement for the rest (most Fable parts have modifiers, so the _vid path rarely pays off);
  - lockstep apply_scale before a part's first stroke;
  - an 'owned' mode for dyntopo, plus a per-part re-bake after dyntopo;
  - a 7-op journal with rev/409, and undo that must also sync into Blender.
- Each of these is a stage failure mode.
- Its parity harness is hedged ('if feasible'), although it has been shown to work.
- It does not densify at export, so sculpting runs at viewport density.
- About 31 h of milestones with the heaviest server and bridge work gives it the lowest effort realism.
- It relies on a deep fork of two-week-old Sculptor internals (initFromWelded, material ids, mask and undo hooks inside split/collapse).

grafts: From web-truth: take the parity harness as-is. Copy plan/parity/blender_ref.py to scripts/blender-ref.py and add test/sculpt-parity.test.js. Keep its tricks: temp_override on the factory VIEW_3D, bpy.ops.ed.undo_push before mode_set, override_location=True, no rv3d.update(), and brush.unprojected_size set to the diameter. Replace the dabs one element at a time with ov=1. Acceptance: at most 2% for kernel brushes and at most 5% for plane and area-centre brushes. This replaces best-hybrid's claim that parity 'can't be automated' (the reference JSONs already exist under plan/parity/ref).

From web-truth: accumulate-off semantics as a written rule for the core. Raycast each dab and read area normals and inflate normals from the stroke-start surface, not the live one. The port error dropped from 4.1% to 1.5% because of this.

From web-truth: detect symmetry at export with a KDTree self-match across the root's X/Y planes, and merge the result with holo_sym from the Mirror modifiers. Fable often builds symmetric models without a Mirror modifier. Announce the detected axis by voice ('mirror Z on').

From blender-truth: turn pressure off by default (p=1, exactly Blender with a mouse). When it is on, feed Blender's own per-brush pressure curves, and keep best-hybrid's [0.5,1] hand multiplier only as an option. Add the Windows Ink PointerEvent.pressure path in mouse mode, so brush feel can be compared with Blender without webcam noise.
