From web-truth and blender-truth: in-browser dyntopo is the first stretch item. Use Sculptor r186 split/collapse in constant-detail mode on untextured, single-material parts. The edge length floor is the part's original mean edge length, which avoids the measured 1M-to-801k coarsening. Disable it for the brushes Blender disallows. Pair it with web-truth's instant in-browser simple subdivision on welded edges (keeps UVs), so 'add detail' works even while Blender is busy.

From web-truth: in the hand mapping, a second-hand fist gives temporary Smooth (Blender's Shift), and two-hand pitch is added alongside yaw. GestureRecognizer runs in a worker if profiling shows frames over 16 ms.

From web-truth: keep the last few pre-change scenes in page memory, so 'undo' after a Fable build swaps back instantly without waiting on a Blender .blend restore (the .blend restore can run in the background).

From blender-truth: Fable-build route. Send voice recolours to Fable by default, as the user asked, and keep best-hybrid's local set_material fast path behind an explicit 'quick' setting. Filter the Material.use_nodes deprecation warnings out of exec output.

Lazy mouse at webcam rate (all plans): Blender's factor 0.9 is applied per input event, and mouse events arrive at more than 120 Hz. Normalise the lazy factor to time, for example factor^(dt/8 ms), so hand input at about 30 Hz doesn't lag.
fatal_flaws: No plan has a truly fatal flaw. All three port the same Blender kernels onto proven MIT mesh infrastructure and reuse measured prototypes.

web-truth (serious, design-level): stateless Blender re-imports the web GLB on every change. That strips every part's modifier stack, bakes procedural materials into images and triangulates quads. Fable's ability to make iterative bpy edits then degrades with each voice change, which undercuts the Fable-builds-detail loop the user asked for.

blender-truth (serious, execution risk): it juggles too many sync states for a hackathon stage. There are two write paths, positions by _vid and mesh replacement; the _vid path rarely applies because Fable parts carry modifiers. There is also lockstep apply_scale, an 'owned' dyntopo mode with a re-bake, a 7-op journal with rev/409, and undo that must sync into Blender. Each one is a place where the web and Blender can silently disagree mid-demo.

best-hybrid (factual error, easily fixed): it states that exact numeric parity with Blender cannot be automated yet. The web-truth harness in plan/parity already does it (21 references; I reproduced about 1.4-1.5% error). Without grafting that harness, the '1:1 with Blender' claim rests only on formula unit tests.

designs.name: Holomodel Clay: the web model is the source of truth, sculpting matches Blender and is tested against real Blender, and Blender runs headless as stateless compute for Fable
designs.one_paragraph: The model lives in the web page as the GLB Blender exported, loaded untouched (metres) under a display parent that scales it into the head-tracked box. Parts are keyed by the holo_id custom property, which survives three.js renaming. Hand sculpting runs on a forked copy of three.js r186's MIT Sculptor. That fork supplies the welded topology, octree, partial normal/GPU updates and edge split/collapse. On top of it sits a GPL-3.0 layer paraphrased from Blender's sculpt code at commit 235621e: the stroke engine (spacing, overlap factor, lazy mouse), the StrokeCache (strength-squared per-brush multipliers, area normal and centre, original data), the per-vertex factor pipeline (mask, front-face, hardness, 10 falloff presets), symmetry passes, auto-smooth, and 19 brush kernels. It is verified against real Blender. I confirmed that headless Blender 5.2.1 runs the actual Essentials brushes through bpy.ops.sculpt.brush_stroke, so every JS kernel is tested against Blender's own output. A 60-line JS Draw/Inflate port already lands within 1.4-1.5% of Blender's displacement. Fable meshes stay intact while you sculpt. Brushes edit a welded proxy (welded by the _vid attribute Blender exports). Results are copied back into the original render mesh, so UV seams, material borders, textures and hard edges never crack or crease. Blender is one warm `blender -b` process owned by the server and treated as stateless compute. A "make" request starts from an empty scene. A "change" request imports the page's current GLB (with your sculpts) into a fresh scene; Fable 5.1 edits it with bpy, looks at renders of the exported GLB, and the result is exported back. That export bakes modifiers and procedural materials and stamps ids and symmetry hints, and the page swaps it in as an undoable step. Voice (ElevenLabs), research, Sentry, versions (now GLBs in MongoDB Atlas GridFS) and the command grammar are kept. The hand-as-Blender-mouse mode, GUI Blender and the old part-list generator are removed.

designs.name: HoloSculpt, Blender-truth edition: Fable builds in an invisible Blender, you sculpt the result in our three.js window, and every hand edit is written back into the .blend
designs.one_paragraph: One headless Blender, owned by our server, holds the real model: a .blend with Fable's live modifiers, procedural materials and named objects. Nobody ever sees Blender's window. Fable 5.1 builds and changes that scene by writing bpy code, checking renders of exactly what the web will receive, and fixing problems. After every step the server exports a GLB, and the three.js workbench in Edge loads it. There the user sculpts with webcam hands and voice, using an engine that copies Blender's sculpt mode: its stroke engine, its per-vertex weight pipeline and its brush kernels, translated to JS from the pinned source at commit 235621e and filled with the real Essentials 5.2.1 preset values. That layer sits on a forked copy of the MIT SculptorMesh from three r186, which provides the octree, neighbour rings, partial normal and GPU updates, and split/collapse dynamic topology. Imported Fable parts stay textured and uncracked while you sculpt: each part gets a welded sculpt copy (proxy) that maps back to the split render mesh, keyed by a `_vid` attribute or by position. After each stroke the edits go back into Blender as raw binary arrays: positions by `_vid` take 4.5 ms for 8k vertices and 24.5 ms for 164k. The first sculpt of a part with modifiers replaces its mesh once. The next spoken change ("make the frame gold") therefore reaches Fable with the sculpt already in the .blend. Voice, ElevenLabs, research, the texture tool, Sentry, the command parser and MongoDB/GridFS versions all stay. Each version now stores both the .blend and the GLB. The hand-as-Blender-mouse code, the GUI add-on installer and the old part-list generator are deleted.

designs.name: HoloModel v3: Fable builds in a hidden Blender, you sculpt it by hand with Blender's own brushes
designs.one_paragraph:
Blender becomes an invisible engine owned by our Node server: one warm `blender -b --factory-startup` process running the bridge add-on. Claude Fable 5.1 builds and changes models there. It writes bpy code, looks at renders of exactly the GLB the web will get, and fixes what it sees. Each finished build goes into our three.js workbench in Edge as a GLB ready for sculpting: modifiers evaluated, every part keyed by a holo_id custom property, coarse parts temporarily subdivided and procedural colours baked. The user edits it there with webcam hands and voice.

Sculpting runs on our own engine, holosculpt, a GPL-3.0 JavaScript port of Blender's sculpt pipeline:
- stroke spacing with overlap normalisation, and the lazy-mouse stabiliser
- squared strength with per-brush multipliers, hardness and the 10 falloff presets
- area normal and brush plane, auto-smooth, object-space symmetry, per-stroke undo
- the brush kernels (Draw, Clay, Clay Strips, the Plane family, Inflate, Crease/Blob, Pinch, Layer, Grab, Elastic Grab, Snake Hook, Smooth/Enhance, Mask)
- Blender 5.2.1 Essentials presets loaded from JSON

It sculpts a welded copy (proxy) of each part, so UV seams, hard edges, materials and textures survive. three-mesh-bvh (MIT) does picking and brush queries.

Hand edits go back into Blender as binary packets before any Fable change, version save or restore, so "make the lid gold" never loses a sculpt. Versions (GLB + .blend) go to MongoDB Atlas, voice uses ElevenLabs, and Sentry traces everything. The renderer stays ours, so the Pepper's-ghost hologram and the Kinect can plug in later.
